user_query: What explains DeepWalk’s weaker Macro-F1 than EdgeCluster on Flickr when the training ratio is only 3%, despite having more labeled data?
llm_response: DeepWalk can still underperform EdgeCluster at a 3% training ratio because its embeddings are learned in an unsupervised way from random walks and may not separate Flickr’s classes well when supervision is very sparse. With only 3% labeled nodes, the classifier has too little labeled signal to fully exploit DeepWalk’s representation, while EdgeCluster’s clustering-based features can align better with the graph’s community structure and class boundaries. So the weaker Macro-F1 is explained by representation quality and class separability, not simply by the amount of labeled data available.
llm_confidence_reasoning: This explanation is consistent with how DeepWalk and EdgeCluster work and with the reported comparison, but the exact dataset-specific cause is inferred rather than directly verified from the prompt.
